The Artist

Guennadi Maslov

Photographer, artist, and educator. Originally from Ukraine, working between Eastern Europe and the United States.

StatementBiographyAchievements

Artist Statement

My work is a translation. It is an attempt to translate the verse of life encounters into the poetry of photography — an attempt to catch the fluid material of the subconscious and put it on a somewhat more stable base of photographic paper.

My work is a reconciliation — an effort to reconcile the Eastern and Western halves of my brain.

My work is an illustration — a never-ending quest to illustrate the fragile dualities of human nature.

Biography

Originally from Ukraine, Guennadi Maslov has nearly 28 years of professional experience in the United States and Europe as a photographer, artist and photo educator. In addition to his artistic work, Maslov teaches photography at area colleges and exhibits his photographs locally, nationally, and internationally.

He often visits his native Ukraine, where, as the photographer puts it, “Common nostalgia often leads to personal artistic discoveries.”

Portfolio  ›  Ukrainian Time

Ukrainian Time

It helps to be far from my elusive heroes. I discover it again and again every year. Two or three weeks are enough. After that you have to go home and start to sort out what you have just seen. Because what you saw in that vast and mysterious part of the world called Eastern Europe, is always psychologically huge.

My heroes live by very different rules. They often must compromise. Honor and money, honesty and greed, health and pleasure, memory and truth. From all of this, I derive my own compromise – that between art and document.

Blog

On returning to the borderland

October 2026 · Guennadi Maslov

It helps to be far from my elusive heroes. I discover it again and again every year. Two or three weeks are enough. After that you have to go home and start to sort out what you have just seen…

At times I ask myself the same questions. And most often I arrive at this answer: for me, Eastern Europe today is the place where human nerve endings come as close to the surface as nowhere else.
